title: Switchback handoff hackpad
content:
Quick context
- Shift: Switchback (overnight -> morning)
- Notes are a messy working list; copy relevant bits into the canonical runbook if they work.
- Recent pattern: intermittent latency spikes from routing layer when A/B rollouts overlap with Dedicated burst events.

Current state summary (as of last check 02:10 UTC)
- All major services: green except route-proxy (p99 latency 550ms last 15m, baseline ~90ms).
- No P1 alerts open. One P2: route-proxy p99 elevated.
- GPU pools: Dedicated-east-1 at 92% util, spillover to hosted available.

Immediate actions I took during the spike (timestamped)
- 01:42 UTC: scaled route-proxy deployment +2 replicas (kubectl scale deploy/route-proxy -n infra --replicas=6). Latency dropped to ~220ms after ~30s.
- 01:48 UTC: noticed autoscaler on Dedicated-east-1 not triggering fast enough due to mis-set cool-down (suspect recent autoscaler-prop PR). Opened PR link above.
- 02:05 UTC: temporarily increased routing fallback weight to hosted-variant (route-control -> set-weight model-variant-hosted 0.2). Stabilized traffic.

Short checklist for you on handoff
- Check route-proxy p99, p95, error rate on dashboard (Dash: infra/routing/route-proxy) — if p99 > 400ms for >5m: scale +2, then if still high, set fallback to hosted-variant weight 0.25.
- Verify Dedicated pool utilization (console: dedicated/pools/east-1) — if > 88% and latency rising, flip burst-capacity on (UI) or run: aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name dedicated-east-1-burst
- Look for recent rollout events (console: rollouts) — if two rollouts in parallel, pause the lower-priority one and drain it.
- If you see GPU OOM on serving nodes: restart the most recent model-dyno pod, then revert to previous quantized build if failures persist (see runbook GPU-OOM snippets below).

Commands / snippets I keep in pocket
- k get pods -n infra -o wide | grep route-proxy
- kubectl logs deploy/route-proxy -n infra --tail=200 | grep -i timeout
- curl -sS https://route-proxy.internal/health | jq .
- curl -X POST https://routing-control.internal/set-weight -d '{"model_variant":"hosted","weight":0.25}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $HANDOFF_TOKEN'
- aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace Redwood/Serving --metric-name TokenLatency --dimensions Name=service,Value=route-proxy --statistics p99 --start-time $(date -u -d '10 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --period 60

Temporary mitigations that worked last week (notes for triage)
- Short-term: lowering model-variant batch size from 64->32 on heavy tails reduced p99 by ~30% (apply to variant:test-batch-32). Caveat: increases cost per token.
- If CPU pressure on route-proxy observed, switch to v2 image (route-proxy:v2.1.7) — v2 has a fix for connection churn.
- For KV cache thrashing: rotate the cache key prefix for the problematic customer if you can identify it (metrics -> cache/hits -> high miss rate per tenant).

Escalation contacts (if you need human help)
- Marcus Li (on-call infra lead) — Slack @marcus / cell +1-415-555-0182 (only if scaling or infra-autoscaler broken).
- Priya N. (runtime) — Slack @priya / cell +1-650-555-0199 (model-serving bugs, GPU OOM).
- Pager: eng-oncall (normal) / eng-crash (critical).

Known rough edges and TODOs (drafts for a better runbook)
- Autoscaler cool-down configuration: PR 1834 fixes; needs canary rollout and observability hooks.
- Routing control API should support staged weight changes (currently instant; causes blips). Draft API spec: routing-control#staged-weight in GH issue tracker.
- Add a short play for "reduce per-tenant latency" that documents steps to identify noisy tenant and throttle their routing weight.

Incident snippets to keep in memory (mini-retros)
- 2025-10-22 GPU OOM cascade: root cause was a quantization mismatch in the new model flavor; hotfix: rollback to q8_0 profile and pin model-tag. Action: add a preflight check for quantized model size in CI.
- 2025-11-16 routing spike during Dedicated failover: autoscaler cool-down prevented new capacity; workaround: manual start refresh and set fallback weight.

Personal handoff suggestions (how I like to do it)
- I leave the most recent timeline at the top, unlink the noisy stuff, and mark TODOs as ACTION items so the next person doesn't chase cold leads.
- If you make a config change, add a one-line rollback note here and in the config PR description.

ACTIONs for morning shift (my recommended order)
- 1) Re-check route-proxy p99 and confirm fallback weight is correct.
- 2) Inspect dedicated-east-1 autoscaler logs (cloudwatch group /aws/autoscaler/dedicated-east-1) for any 5xx or throttling.
- 3) Run a brief load test against hosted-variant to validate it can absorb 20% traffic without tail latencies.
- 4) If stable, update the incident ticket (JIRA-INVEST-842) with steps taken and close P2.

Loose notes / scribbles for later cleaning
- Consider adding a sticky flag in console to pin the preferred fallback model for each customer tier.
- Short-term: add a small synthetic test that runs every minute to detect route-proxy contention before it hits p99.

End of page. Save to canonical runbook when stable.

-- Aisha
(leave a line under your name with the main change you did during your shift, e.g. "scaled route-proxy +2 at 01:42 UTC, set hosted fallback weight 0.25 at 02:05 UTC")
